marks.gloss_en: אתון מהכא מתניתו לה, אנן מהכא מתנינן לה: ואתה תשמע השמים וסלחת
Ze'eiri of Dihavat to Ravina: you learn it from there; we learn it from here: 'then hear in heaven and forgive the sin...' (1 Kings 8:36)
אנן מהכא מתנינן לה: ועצר את השמים... ואבדתם מהרה
R' Tanchum son of R' Chiya: rain is withheld only if [the enemies of] Israel have become liable to destruction (Job 24:19)
מאי משמע? תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: בשביל דברים שציויתי אתכם בימות החמה ולא עשיתם -- יגזלו מכם מימי שלג בימות הגשמים
Rav Chisda: rain is withheld only for the neglect of terumot and tithes (Job 24:19)
רב יוסף אמר מהכא: ועתה לא ראו אור... ואין אור אלא תורה
Rav Yosef: from here -- 'and now they do not see the light, it is bright in the skies' (Job 37:21); 'light' is Torah (Prov 6:23)
אי הוו סנו טפי הוו גמירי -- had they been ugly they would have been more learned (= p_rybch_sanu)
R' Yehoshua ben Chananya: had they been ugly, they would have been more learned
R' Chama b. R' Chanina: the day of rain is as great as the day heaven and earth were created (Isa 45:8) -- 'I created it', not 'them'
Rav Oshaya: the day of rain is great, for even salvation multiplies on it -- 'let the earth open and salvation be fruitful' (Isa 45:8)
R' Shimon ben Pazi: rain is withheld only for tellers of slander (Prov 25:23)
Rav Hamnuna: rain is withheld only for the brazen-faced (Jer 3:3)
Rabba bar Rav Huna: whoever is brazen-faced may be called wicked (Prov 21:29)
Rav Ketina: rain is withheld only for neglect of Torah -- 'through slothfulness the rafters sink' (Eccl 10:18); mach is poor (Lev 27:8), mekareh is the Holy One (Ps 104:3)
R' Ami: rain is withheld only for the sin of robbery -- 'for the palms He covers the light' (Job 36:32); palms is violence (Jonah 3:8), light is rain (Job 37:11)
its remedy: increase prayer -- 'and He commands it bemafgia' (Job 36:32), and pegia is prayer (Jer 7:16)
R' Ami: 'if the iron is blunt and he does not whet the edge' (Eccl 10:10) -- a sky blunt as iron from bringing dew and rain is because of the generation's corrupt deeds
their remedy: let them strengthen themselves in [prayer for] mercy (Eccl 10:10); all the more so had their deeds been proper from the start
